screening_decisions.reason: RCT randomly allocating 42 frozen-shoulder patients to intra-articular steroids, mobilisations, ice therapy or no treatment; all were taught pendular exercises. The trial compares manual therapy (mobilisations) plus exercise against other interventions in the target population, meeting the review’s design, population and intervention criteria.

Observational incidence and management study in Dutch general practice (n=349 incident cases). It is not an RCT or quasi-randomised trial and does not evaluate manual therapy or exercise interventions for adhesive capsulitis in a controlled design.
Narrative review of textbook principles of joint mobilization for athletic trainers. Not a primary clinical trial; no patient population or comparative intervention data.

Open RCT comparing physical therapies plus arthrographic distension with intra-articular steroid versus physical therapies alone. Both groups received the same physical therapies (therapeutic exercises, TENS, IRR) as a co-intervention; the experimental variable is distension/steroid injection, not manual therapy or exercise. Therefore it does not address the review’s comparisons of interest.
Methodological study systematically reviewing cohorts of RCTs to compare protocols/registry entries with published reports. Not a clinical trial of manual therapy or exercise for adhesive capsulitis.

Explicitly described as a randomized controlled trial evaluating deep transverse friction massage (manual therapy) and capsular stretching in patients with idiopathic adhesive capsulitis. Meets the required population, intervention and study design criteria.

RCT randomly allocating frozen-shoulder patients to two different exercise programs (glenohumeral ROM exercises with or without scapulothoracic exercises). Compares exercise versus a different type of exercise in the target population, fitting the review’s inclusion criteria.

Randomized multiple-treatment trial comparing end-range mobilization, mid-range mobilization and mobilization with movement in subjects with frozen shoulder syndrome. Mobilization is a key manual therapy intervention of interest, and the study design is an RCT.

Study comparing proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) movement patterns versus conventional free exercises for range of motion in chronic peri-arthritis (frozen shoulder). It appears to be a comparative clinical study of exercise interventions in the target population. Included conservatively for full-text verification of randomized design.

Pilot RCT using block randomization to compare antero-posterior versus postero-anterior glide mobilization in primary adhesive capsulitis. Directly compares two manual therapy techniques in the relevant population.
Two-stage cross-sectional prevalence survey (n=9,696) of upper-limb musculoskeletal disorders. Not a trial; no intervention comparison.
Multiple-subject case report (n=7) describing end-range mobilization techniques. Not an RCT or quasi-randomised trial; lacks a control group and randomization.

Placebo-controlled RCT randomizing 93 subjects with adhesive capsulitis to corticosteroid + supervised physiotherapy, corticosteroid alone, saline + supervised physiotherapy, or saline alone. Includes a supervised physiotherapy (exercise/manual therapy) arm versus placebo, directly relevant to the review’s comparisons.

Randomized, placebo-controlled trial comparing manual therapy and directed exercise versus sham ultrasound after joint distension in adhesive capsulitis. Relevant population and compares manual therapy plus exercise against a sham control.
Observational study within primary care evaluating the measurement properties (responsiveness) of the Shoulder Disability Questionnaire. Not a trial of manual therapy or exercise interventions.

Study of 75 frozen-shoulder patients treated with physical therapy, acupuncture, or both. No mention of randomization or controlled design; uneven group sizes (30/30/15) suggest non-random allocation. Does not meet the RCT/quasi-RCT criterion.
Systematic review and cost-effectiveness analysis. Not a primary RCT or quasi-randomised trial.

Study comparing anterior versus posterior glide mobilisation techniques for internal rotation in shoulder adhesive capsulitis. Appears to be a comparative clinical study of manual therapy techniques in the target population. Included conservatively for full-text verification of randomized design.
Methodological cohort study examining outcome reporting bias across RCTs included in Cochrane reviews. Not a clinical trial of manual therapy or exercise for adhesive capsulitis.

Title refers to frozen shoulder, but the abstract describes an inception cohort study of patients recently diagnosed with multiple sclerosis investigating social role performance. Mismatched or incorrect abstract. In any case, it is not an RCT of manual therapy or exercise for adhesive capsulitis.

Randomized clinical trial (n=87) comparing corticosteroid injection, physiotherapy, and combination therapy in frozen shoulder. Physiotherapy constitutes an exercise/manual therapy intervention, and the trial compares it against other interventions in the target population.

RCT randomizing 40 adhesive capsulitis patients to Cyriax approach (deep friction massage and mobilisation exercises) versus conventional physical therapy (hot pack, short wave diathermy). Compares manual therapy plus exercise versus other physical therapy modalities in the relevant population.
Prospective observational study following 49 patients with frozen shoulder syndrome for 5–10 years to describe natural history. No intervention or control group; not an RCT.
Methodological paper proposing statistical measures (H, R, I²) for quantifying heterogeneity in meta-analysis. Not a primary clinical trial.
Book chapter discussing types, avoidance and detection of reporting biases. Not a primary clinical trial of manual therapy or exercise for adhesive capsulitis.
Prospective observational study of natural history without a randomized comparison of manual therapy or exercise interventions.
RCT of patients with adhesive capsulitis comparing joint mobilization plus active exercises versus active exercises alone; meets selection criteria.

RCT in adults with adhesive capsulitis including a physical therapy modalities arm; physiotherapy for frozen shoulder typically involves exercise and/or manual therapy, so this is included conservatively at title/abstract screening.
Electromyographic biomechanics study assessing muscle activation during exercises in subjects with and without shoulder pathology; not a randomized treatment trial for adhesive capsulitis.
Comparative study of chronic shoulder pain of mixed etiologies (trauma, degeneration, etc.); not restricted to adhesive capsulitis and design is not clearly an eligible RCT.

RCT of adults with adhesive capsulitis comparing local steroid injection versus physical therapy measures; physical therapy for this condition typically comprises exercise and/or mobilisation, meeting the intervention criteria.
Cochrane handbook chapter on interpreting results; not a primary clinical trial.
Retrospective study assessing response to various treatments without randomization; does not meet RCT or quasi-RCT design requirements.
Randomised controlled study comparing two manual therapy mobilisation techniques (Mulligan’s vs Maitland’s) in adhesive capsulitis; meets selection criteria.
Cochrane handbook chapter on presenting results; not a primary clinical trial.
Population-based epidemiological study measuring consultation prevalence for shoulder pain; not a treatment trial.
RCT of shoulder periarthritis comparing iontophoresis and phonophoresis (electrotherapy modalities), not manual therapy or exercise interventions for adhesive capsulitis.
Prospective randomised observer-blind trial of patients with painful stiff shoulder (frozen shoulder) comparing local steroid injection, physiotherapy, or both; meets RCT and intervention criteria.

Double-blind RCT of frozen shoulder subjects comparing electroacupuncture plus exercise, interferential electrotherapy plus exercise, and no treatment; includes an exercise intervention arm and meets selection criteria.
RCT of adults with adhesive capsulitis comparing ibuprofen alone versus ibuprofen combined with physical therapy; meets population, design, and intervention criteria.
Randomised controlled trial of chronic adhesive capsulitis comparing exercises and ultrasound with or without end-range mobilisation techniques; manual therapy and exercise are evaluated.
Randomized clinical trial in adhesive capsulitis comparing anterior versus posterior glide joint mobilisation techniques alongside ultrasound and ergometer exercise; meets selection criteria.
RCT of shoulder capsulitis comparing intra-articular triamcinolone and/or standardized physiotherapy versus placebo; physiotherapy provides exercise/manual therapy content eligible for this review.
Prospective randomised trial of adhesive capsulitis comparing manipulation under anaesthesia, peri-articular injection, and physiotherapy; includes manual therapy and physiotherapy arms.
Systematic review of interventions for frozen shoulder; not a primary RCT or quasi-RCT.
Cochrane handbook chapter on meta-analysis methods; not a primary clinical trial.
Randomized controlled study of limited glenohumeral joint mobility from adhesive capsulitis comparing joint mobilization versus self-exercises; directly evaluates manual therapy and exercise.

Prospective clinical trial (systematically allocated, i.e., quasi-randomised) of stage 2–3 adhesive capsulitis comparing chiropractic manipulation plus exercise versus mobilization plus exercise; eligible quasi-randomised trial with manual therapy and exercise.
Randomized controlled trial of adhesive capsulitis comparing high-grade versus low-grade mobilization techniques; eligible manual therapy comparison.
Single-blinded pilot RCT of adhesive capsulitis comparing home-care programme versus home-care plus passive joint mobilisation; evaluates manual therapy as an adjunct.
